chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala from Aban from 'Isa ibn 'Abdullah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the hunting of the Magians, so he said: There is no harm if they give it to you alive, and the fish as well; otherwise, do not accept their testimony unless you witness it yourself.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat game hunted by Zoroastrians according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in *al-Istibsar* clarifies the status of Magians as 'People of the Book' regarding their hunted game, permitting consumption if the prey is presented alive, thereby affirming the validity of their slaughter in this specific context. The hadith further establishes a nuanced legal principle where their general testimony is rejected due to potential religious bias, unless validated by a Muslim witness, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential approach to *ahl al-kitab* in daily transactions and evidence.
